reading.body:
DartPoints Columbia publishes 2 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 2 MW is roughly 50 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it is roughly 200 racks. Either figure places this as a small facility. No redundancy tier, power utilization effectiveness rating, or cooling architecture is published, so the suitability of the physical infrastructure for sustained GPU workloads cannot be assessed from available data.

Among the 14 data center facilities mapped in South Carolina, DartPoints Columbia is the only one for which this site holds a published megawatt figure, giving it a nominal rank of first in the state by that measure. That ranking reflects a data gap more than a capacity lead: the other 13 mapped facilities publish no IT load figure, so no state-level comparison is possible. South Carolina's total published IT capacity across all mapped facilities is 2 MW, which is this campus alone.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the honest answer is that 2 MW of IT capacity is below the threshold at which hyperscale or frontier-model training campuses are typically measured, and no published specifications confirm the power density, redundancy, or connectivity needed for large accelerator deployments. The campus could support inference workloads or smaller training clusters, but no published data confirms it is configured for either. A reader with genuine interest in deploying AI infrastructure here would need to request specifications that are not on the operator's published page.
